questions.q: Who is the architect known for the dictum "Form follows function"?
questions.n: Known as the father of skyscrapers, he coined this famous phrase in his 1896 article.

questions.q: Which Japanese architect is famous for his "Haiku" effect—the use of raw concrete, light, and natural elements?
questions.n: His work is characterized by critical regionalism and the masterful use of 'smooth-as-silk' concrete.

questions.q: Who is the architect of the EDSA Shrine (Shrine of Mary, Queen of Peace)?
questions.n: A National Artist known for Neo-vernacular architecture and the use of indigenous Filipino materials.

questions.q: Which National Architect of the Philippines is famous for the design of the CCP (Cultural Center of the Philippines) and the Church of the Holy Sacrifice (UP Diliman)?
questions.n: He is famous for his use of floating volumes and the expressive use of concrete.

questions.q: Which Japanese architect designed the St. Mary’s Cathedral in Tokyo and the Hiroshima Peace Memorial?
questions.n: A Pritzker prize winner who combined traditional Japanese styles with modernism.

questions.q: Which architect is known for his strict adherence to white neomodernist designs, as seen in the Getty Center?
questions.n: He is a member of 'The New York Five' and is famous for his consistent use of the color white and geometric clarity.

questions.q: In ancient Egyptian architecture, what is the rectangular, flat-topped funerary mound with sloped sides that preceded the pyramid?
questions.n: This was the standard type of tomb in early dynastic Egypt for pharaohs and nobles.

questions.q: What is the term for architectural structures carved directly into solid rock, such as the Treasury at Petra or the temples at Abu Simbel?
questions.n: This describes architecture where a structure is created by excavating it out of solid natural rock.

questions.q: The focus of Egyptian architecture was primarily centered on what concept?
questions.n: Their belief in the afterlife dictated the permanence of their tombs and funerary monuments.

questions.q: While Roman architecture focused on religious and civic power, what was the primary focus of Greek architecture?
o: Natural phenomena and physical perfection (Optical illusions/Refinement)
questions.n: Greek architects used entasis and other subtle adjustments to achieve perceived mathematical perfection.

questions.q: Who is the Filipino architect recognized as a pioneer in the design of modern hospital facilities in the Philippines?
questions.n: He is widely cited in board exams for his contributions to hospital planning and design.

questions.q: Which architect is famous for designing the iconic "Istana Nurul Iman" (The Sultan's Palace in Brunei)?
questions.n: This massive project is one of his most significant international commissions.

questions.q: Which Finnish architect was famous not only for buildings but also for his significant work in glassware (e.g., Savoy Vase) and textiles?
questions.n: His work was a 'humanizing' modernism that extended to furniture, lighting, and glassware.

questions.q: Which cathedral features the tallest Gothic vault in the world (though it later collapsed)?
questions.n: Architects pushed the structural limits to reach a vault height of 48 meters, leading to structural failures.

questions.q: Which French Gothic cathedral is world-renowned for its extensive and beautifully preserved 13th-century rose windows?
questions.n: Considered the high point of French Gothic art, famous for its blue stained glass.

questions.q: Which cathedral is unique for having "two choir areas" or a double-ended plan layout?
questions.n: The double-transept and extended choir plan give it a distinctive double-ended appearance.

questions.q: What is the world's largest aquarium located in Scottsdale, Arizona, often cited for its "OdySea Voyager" attraction?
questions.n: A high-tech aquarium in the desert known for its rotating viewing platform.

questions.q: What is the largest aquarium in Europe, known for its distinctive "Blue Planet" design?
questions.n: Located in Copenhagen, Denmark; its architecture resembles a whirlpool.

questions.q: What is the term for a monumental structure with a square or triangular base and sloping sides that meet in a point at the top?
questions.n: The iconic funerary structure of the Old Kingdom Pharaohs.

questions.q: The Parthenon in Athens is the ultimate example of which architectural focus?
o: The Greek focus on natural phenomena and mathematical harmony.
The Roman focus on interior grandeur
questions.n: Every part of the Parthenon follows a ratio to achieve what the Greeks saw as visual perfection.

questions.q: Under SPP 202, what is the first phase of Regular Design Services where the architect illustrates the concepts for the project?
questions.n: The phase involving the conceptual framework and preliminary drawings.

questions.q: In which phase does the architect prepare the final set of technical drawings, specifications, and bill of quantities?
questions.n: The architect produces the documents necessary for bidding and building the project.

questions.q: If the Project Construction Cost (PCC) is 50,000,000 PHP and the basic fee is 6%, how much is the total basic fee?
questions.n: Calculated as 50,000,000 multiplied by 0.06.

questions.q: Upon completion of the Schematic Design Phase, what percentage of the Architect's basic fee is typically due (cumulative)?
questions.n: Standard practice dictates a total of 15% cumulative after the schematic phase is approved.

questions.q: Upon completion of the Contract Documents Phase, what is the total cumulative percentage of the basic fee usually paid to the architect?
questions.n: The architect has completed the bulk of the design work, leaving 15% for bidding and construction supervision.

questions.q: What method of compensation is most appropriate for a small, simple project where the final construction cost is hard to predict?
questions.n: A single set amount agreed upon regardless of the final construction cost.

questions.q: What compensation method involves multiplying the actual direct cost by a multiplier to cover overhead and profit?
questions.n: Often used for non-creative work or when the scope is not well-defined.

questions.q: If a client requests a "Retainer," what does this usually cover?
o: Full design of a single-family house
Professional advice on a regular basis without a full design commission.
The purchase of furniture for the client
The cost of building the foundation
questions.n: The architect is 'on call' to provide expert opinion or guidance.

questions.q: Under the SPP, who is responsible for paying for the services of Specialist Consultants?
o: The Owner (but coordinated by the Architect).
questions.n: The owner pays consultants (like structural or MEP engineers) directly or as a separate item.

questions.q: In the computation of the Architect's fee, what does PCC stand for?
questions.n: The total cost of all elements of the project designed or specified by the architect.

questions.q: Under the National Building Code, what is the required width of a "Chaflan" for a corner lot with a street width of 3.60 meters?
o: 4.00 meters (Standard for streets less than 3.60m is 4m chaflan).
questions.n: The NBC requires a 4-meter chaflan for street widths less than 3.6 meters.

questions.q: According to PD 957, what is the minimum front setback for a residential lot?
questions.n: PD 957 (Open Market/Middle Class) requires more generous setbacks than socialized housing.

questions.q: Under BP 220, what is the minimum front setback for an Economic/Socialized housing unit?
questions.n: BP 220 allows for smaller setbacks to maximize density in socialized projects.

questions.q: For a subdivision project with an area of 1 hectare (10,000 sqm), what is the minimum area requirement for Parks and Playgrounds?
o: 350 sqm (3.5% of gross area for 20-65 units/ha).
questions.n: The requirement scales based on density; 3.5% is the baseline for 20-65 units per hectare.

questions.q: What is the maximum distance of a parking slot from a condominium unit according to standard planning?
questions.n: This is the maximum walking distance usually cited to ensure accessibility and convenience.

questions.q: In BP 344, what is the minimum clear width of a corridor to allow for wheelchair passage?
questions.n: 1.10m is the absolute minimum to allow a wheelchair to navigate clearly.

questions.q: What is the minimum dimensions for a PWD-accessible toilet under BP 344?
questions.n: Standard dimension to accommodate the fixture and the necessary turning space.

questions.q: Under BP 344, what is the maximum height of a "Threshold" that a wheelchair can cross?
o: 25 mm (though usually preferred to be flush).
questions.n: This is the maximum allowable bump at doors or transitions.

questions.q: What is the minimum required size for a "Single-Detached" lot in PD 957 (Open Market)?
questions.n: The minimum lot area for single-detached units in open market subdivisions.

questions.q: What is the minimum width of a major road in a PD 957 subdivision?
questions.n: The standard minimum width for a major road serving a project of this type.

questions.q: Which architect is associated with the quote "Modern architecture does not mean the use of new materials, but using materials in a modern way"?
questions.n: His work often showcased traditional Japanese philosophy executed in modern concrete.

questions.q: Who is the architect of the "Church of the Light" in Osaka, Japan?
questions.n: The church is famous for the cross-shaped void in the wall that allows light to enter.

questions.q: In ancient Egyptian architecture, which king built the first Step Pyramid at Saqqara?
questions.n: His architect Imhotep stacked mastabas to create the first pyramid form.

questions.q: What was the primary building material for ancient Greek temples?
questions.n: Abundant local stone allowed for the permanence and precision of Greek orders.

questions.q: Which National Artist for Architecture designed the Coconut Palace?
questions.n: Designed for the Tadhana film festival, it showcases the versatility of the coconut tree.

questions.q: Under the Code of Ethical Conduct, what is the architect's primary responsibility toward the public?
o: To strictly follow the contractor's advice
To ensure the client saves money
To uphold the interest of public health, safety, and welfare.
To make the building look beautiful
questions.n: This is the 'highest' ethical duty of any professional architect.

questions.q: In the design of hospitals, what is the most critical planning consideration for infection control?
o: The color of the scrub suits
Zoning and Airflow (Separation of sterile and non-sterile zones).
questions.n: Effective zoning prevents the cross-contamination of clean and dirty areas.

questions.q: What is the term for the 45-degree angle cut at the corner of a building at a street intersection?
questions.n: The cut-off corner mandated by the National Building Code for visibility.

questions.q: Which architect’s work is characterized by the concept of "Space and Silence"?
questions.n: His minimalist approach creates meditative, quiet environments.

questions.q: What architectural style is characterized by the use of flying buttresses, pointed arches, and ribbed vaults?
questions.n: These three innovations allowed for thinner walls and much larger windows.
